transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I’m here because nobody seems to take it seriously that people at work are secretly targeting my projects, even when I show them the evidence. It’s incredibly frustrating that everyone just dismisses it when the proof is right there. I just want someone to actually listen to what is going on.

How long have you been feeling that people at work are targeting you, and did it start suddenly or build up over time? Have you also noticed hearing voices or having thoughts that feel inserted or controlled by someone else?

It’s been going on for about nine months now, starting gradually after a major cloud migration project last year when I began noticing patterns in the glitches and logs. As for hearing voices or having thoughts put into my head, absolutely not—my thoughts are entirely my own, and this is strictly about the physical actions that other team is taking against my work.

Aside from believing your coworkers are targeting your projects, have you had any other experiences like seeing or hearing things others don’t, or has anyone noticed your speech or behavior becoming disorganized or more withdrawn? Have you had trouble keeping up with daily work or self-care because of this?

No, I don't experience any hallucinations or disorganized behavior; outside of protecting my work, I handle my tickets, pay bills, and meet my cousin for pho just fine. However, I have pulled back from team social events and basketball because I'm constantly on guard, and HR did warn me about making accusations in meetings.
Do you believe your coworkers are using special technology or impossible methods to control your projects or influence you, or is it more that they are sabotaging you in ordinary, real-world ways?

There is nothing magical or impossible about what they are doing; it is straightforward, real-world sabotage. They are slipping bad code directly into my branches, exploiting glitches to make me look incompetent, and monitoring my personal accounts to track my moves. It is all right there in the logs, and it could easily be proven if anyone actually bothered to look at the data.

Have you ever felt that strangers, TV, the internet, or your devices are sending you special messages about you or controlling your thoughts or actions in any way? Or is this only about specific coworkers sabotaging you in ordinary ways?

No, absolutely not—that sounds completely ridiculous, and I don't believe the TV or strangers are sending me messages. This is strictly about a competing tech team at my company covertly sabotaging my code, slipping bad code into my branches, and monitoring my personal accounts to make me look incompetent.

During these past nine months, have you had any periods lasting several days or more when you felt unusually depressed, or unusually energized with much less need for sleep, racing thoughts, or risky behavior? I want to know whether these beliefs only happen during those mood changes or even when your mood is otherwise normal.

No, I haven't experienced any major mood swings, depression, or racing thoughts. I do stay up late sometimes to check the logs, but that's purely out of stress and the need to protect my code from being sabotaged. My mood is generally normal, just highly stressed by what's happening at work.

The belief has persisted for about nine months, is systematized and non-bizarre (ordinary workplace sabotage and monitoring), and there are repeated denials of hallucinations, thought insertion/control, reference phenomena, disorganization, and prominent mood episodes. Functioning is largely preserved outside the delusion, with only social withdrawal and workplace conflict related to the belief. These features continue to support F22.0 over schizophrenia-spectrum disorders with broader psychotic symptoms or mood disorders with psychotic symptoms.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports a single, persistent persecutory delusional belief lasting about nine months that coworkers are sabotaging projects and monitoring accounts, with non-bizarre real-world content. Schizophrenia-spectrum features such as hallucinations, thought insertion/control, disorganized speech/behavior, and prominent negative symptoms were denied. There is no evidence that the belief occurs exclusively during mood episodes, and overall functioning is relatively preserved aside from conflict and social withdrawal related to the delusion. This is most consistent with delusional disorder, persecutory type.
